sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ gāś ca yac cānyan manyase vibho tat te dadyāṃ varaṃ vipra na nivartet kratur mama
english: Janamejaya said: Gold, silver, cows, and whatever else you may desire, O lord — all that I would give you as a boon, O brahmin; let my sacrifice not be turned back.

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ gāś ca na tvāṃ rājan vṛṇomy aham satraṃ te viramatv etat svasti mātṛkulasya naḥ
english: Āstīka said: Gold, silver, and cows — none of these do I choose from you, O king. Let this sacrifice of yours be stopped; may there be welfare for our mother's kin.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca āstīkenaivam uktas tu rājā pārikṣitas tadā punaḥ punar uvācedam āstīkaṃ vadatāṃ varam
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed by Āstīka, the king, son of Parīkṣit, then spoke again and again to Āstīka, saying, 'Choose among those who speak the best boon.'

sanskrit: anyaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varaṃ dvijavarottama ayācata na cāpy anyaṃ varaṃ sa bhṛgunandana
english: He said: Choose another boon, good fortune to you, O best of the twice-born. But that son of the Bhṛgu line asked for no other boon.

sanskrit: tato vedavidas tatra sadasyāḥ sarva eva tam rājānam ūcuḥ sahitā labhatāṃ brāhmaṇo varam
english: Then all the learned members of the assembly who were versed in the Vedas together spoke to that king: Let the brahmin receive his boon.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca ye sarpāḥ sarpasatre 'smin patitā havyavāhane teṣāṃ nāmāni sarveṣāṃ śrotum icchāmi sūtaja
english: Śaunaka said: Those serpents that fell into the fire in this snake sacrifice — I wish to hear the names of all of them, O son of the Sūta.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca sahasrāṇi bahūny asmin prayutāny arbudāni ca na śakyaṃ parisaṃkhyātuṃ bahutvād vedavittama
english: The Sūta said: Many thousands, millions, and hundreds of millions — they cannot be fully enumerated because of their great number, O best of Veda-knowers.

sanskrit: yathāsmṛti tu nāmāni pannagānāṃ nibodha me ucyamānāni mukhyānāṃ hutānāṃ jātavedasi
english: Yet as I remember them, hear from me the names of the chief serpents that were offered into the sacred fire, as I speak them.

sanskrit: vāsukeḥ kulajāṃs tāvat prādhānyena nibodha me nīlaraktān sitān ghorān mahākāyān viṣolbaṇān
english: Learn from me first, by way of eminence, those born in Vāsuki's lineage — dark, red, white, terrible, of great bodies, and fierce with venom.

sanskrit: koṭiko mānasaḥ pūrṇaḥ sahaḥ pailo halīsakaḥ picchilaḥ koṇapaś cakraḥ koṇavegaḥ prakālanaḥ
english: Koṭika, Mānasa, Pūrṇa, Saha, Paila, Halīsaka, Picchila, Koṇapa, Cakra, Koṇavega, and Prakālana —

sanskrit: hiraṇyavāhaḥ śaraṇaḥ kakṣakaḥ kāladantakaḥ ete vāsukijā nāgāḥ praviṣṭā havyavāhanam
english: Hiraṇyavāha, Śaraṇa, Kakṣaka, and Kāladantaka — these serpents born of Vāsuki entered the sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: takṣakasya kule jātān pravakṣyāmi nibodha tān pucchaṇḍako maṇḍalakaḥ piṇḍabhettā rabheṇakaḥ
english: Those born in the lineage of Takṣaka I will now declare; hear them: Pucchaṇḍaka, Maṇḍalaka, Piṇḍabhettā, and Rabheṇaka —

sanskrit: ucchikhaḥ suraso draṅgo balaheḍo virohaṇaḥ śilīśalakaro mūkaḥ sukumāraḥ pravepanaḥ
english: Ucchikha, Surasa, Draṅga, Balaheḍa, Virohaṇa, Śilīśalakara, Mūka, Sukumāra, and Pravepana —

sanskrit: mudgaraḥ śaśaromā ca sumanā vegavāhanaḥ ete takṣakajā nāgāḥ praviṣṭā havyavāhanam
english: Mudgara, Śaśaromā, Sumanā, and Vegavāhana — these serpents born of Takṣaka entered the sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: pārāvataḥ pāriyātraḥ pāṇḍaro hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ vihaṃgaḥ śarabho modaḥ pramodaḥ saṃhatāṅgadaḥ
english: Pārāvata, Pāriyātra, Pāṇḍara, Hariṇa, Kṛśa, Vihaṃga, Śarabha, Moda, Pramoda, and Saṃhatāṅgada —

sanskrit: airāvatakulād ete praiviṣṭā havyavāhanam kauravyakulajān nāgāñ śṛṇu me dvijasattama
english: These from the lineage of Airāvata entered the sacrificial fire. Now hear from me the serpents born in the lineage of Kauravya, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: aiṇḍilaḥ kuṇḍalo muṇḍo veṇiskandhaḥ kumārakaḥ bāhukaḥ śṛṅgavegaś ca dhūrtakaḥ pātapātarau
english: Aiṇḍila, Kuṇḍala, Muṇḍa, Veṇiskandha, Kumāraka, Bāhuka, Śṛṅgavega, Dhūrtaka, and the pair Pāta and Pātara —

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrakule jātāñ śṛṇu nāgān yathātatham kīrtyamānān mayā brahman vātavegān viṣolbaṇān
english: Hear in detail the serpents born in the lineage of Dhṛtarāṣṭra as I enumerate them, O brahmin — swift as the wind and fierce with venom.

sanskrit: śaṅkukarṇaḥ piṅgalakaḥ kuṭhāramukhamecakau pūrṇāṅgadaḥ pūrṇamukhaḥ prahasaḥ śakunir hariḥ
english: Śaṅkukarṇa, Piṅgalaka, Kuṭhāramukha, Mecaka, Pūrṇāṅgada, Pūrṇamukha, Prahasa, Śakuni, and Hari —

sanskrit: āmāhaṭhaḥ komaṭhakaḥ śvasano mānavo vaṭaḥ bhairavo muṇḍavedāṅgaḥ piśaṅgaś codrapāragaḥ
english: Āmāhaṭha, Komaṭhaka, Śvasana, Mānava, Vaṭa, Bhairava, Muṇḍavedāṅga, Piśaṅga, and Udrapāraga —

sanskrit: ṛṣabho vegavān nāma piṇḍārakamahāhanū raktāṅgaḥ sarvasāraṅgaḥ samṛddhaḥ pāṭarākṣasau
english: Ṛṣabha, Vegavān, Piṇḍāraka, Mahāhanu, Raktāṅga, Sarvasāraṅga, Samṛddha, and the pair Pāṭa and Rākṣasa —

sanskrit: varāhako vāraṇakaḥ sumitraś citravedikaḥ parāśaras taruṇako maṇiskandhas tathāruṇiḥ
english: Varāhaka, Vāraṇaka, Sumitra, Citravediha, Parāśara, Taruṇaka, Maṇiskandha, and Āruṇi —

sanskrit: iti nāgā mayā brahman kīrtitāḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ prādhānyena bahutvāt tu na sarve parikīrtitāḥ
english: Thus have I enumerated these fame-enhancing serpents, O brahmin — the chief ones principally; not all of them, given their great multitude.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ putrapautrās tu prasavasya ca saṃtatiḥ na śakyāḥ parisaṃkhyātuṃ ye dīptaṃ pāvakaṃ gatāḥ
english: The sons and grandsons of these, and the whole succession of their offspring who entered the blazing fire — they cannot be fully counted.

sanskrit: saptaśīrṣā dviśīrṣāś ca pañcaśīrṣās tathāpare kālānalaviṣā ghorā hutāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Those with seven heads, those with two heads, and others with five heads — terrible, bearing the venom of the fires of time — were offered by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: mahākāyā mahāvīryāḥ śailaśṛṅgasamucchrayāḥ yojanāyāmavistārā dviyojanasamāyatāḥ
english: Of vast body and great might, towering like mountain peaks, a yojana in length and breadth, or stretching two yojanas in extent —

sanskrit: kāmarūpāḥ kāmagamā dīptānalaviṣolbaṇāḥ dagdhās tatra mahāsatre brahmadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ
english: Able to assume any form at will, moving wherever they wished, fierce with the venom of blazing fire — they were burned in that great sacrifice, crushed by the rod of Brahman's curse.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca idam atyadbhutaṃ cānyad āstīkasyānuśuśrumaḥ tathā varaiś chandyamāne rājñā pārikṣitena ha
english: The Sūta said: We have heard of yet another most wonderful thing concerning Āstīka, when the king, son of Parīkṣit, was plying him with boons.

sanskrit: indrahastāc cyuto nāgaḥ kha eva yad atiṣṭhata tataś cintāparo rājā babhūva janamejayaḥ
english: When the serpent slipped from Indra's hand and remained suspended in mid-air, King Janamejaya became deeply anxious.

sanskrit: hūyamāne bhṛśaṃ dīpte vidhivat pāvake tadā na sma sa prāpatad vahnau takṣako bhayapīḍitaḥ
english: Though the fire was burning fiercely and offerings were being made in the proper manner, Takṣaka, tormented by fear, did not fall into the fire.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca kiṃ sūta teṣāṃ viprāṇāṃ mantragrāmo manīṣiṇām na pratyabhāt tadāgnau yan na papāta sa takṣakaḥ
english: Śaunaka said: Why, O Sūta, did the collection of mantras of those wise brahmins fail to work, so that Takṣaka did not then fall into the fire?

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tam indrahastād visrastaṃ visaṃjñaṃ pannagottamam āstīkas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vācas tisro 'bhyudairayat
english: The Sūta said: As that best of serpents slipped from Indra's hand and was losing consciousness, Āstīka raised his voice three times, calling out: Stop! Stop!

sanskrit: vitasthe so 'ntarikṣe 'tha hṛdayena vidūyatā yathā tiṣṭheta vai kaś cid gocakrasyāntarā naraḥ
english: Then that serpent remained stationary in the sky, its heart trembling — just as a man might stand still when caught within a circle of cattle.

sanskrit: tato rājābravīd vākyaṃ sadasyaiś codito bhṛśam kāmam etad bhavatv evaṃ yathāstīkasya bhāṣitam
english: Then the king, strongly urged by the members of the assembly, spoke: Let it be so, as Āstīka has spoken, as he desires.

sanskrit: samāpyatām idaṃ karma pannagāḥ santv anāmayāḥ prīyatām ayam āstīkaḥ satyaṃ sūtavaco 'stu tat
english: Let this rite be concluded; let the serpents be free from harm; let this Āstīka be pleased; and let the words of the Sūta prove true.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdaḥ prītijaḥ samavartata āstīkasya vare datte tathaivopararāma ca
english: Then a cry of rejoicing arose; and when the boon was granted to Āstīka, it likewise came to rest — the sacrifice stopped.

sanskrit: sa yajñaḥ pāṇḍaveyasya rājñaḥ pārikṣitasya ha prītimāṃś cābhavad rājā bhārato janamejayaḥ
english: That sacrifice of the king, the son of Pāṇḍu's line, the son of Parīkṣit — and King Janamejaya of the Bharata race was pleased.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhyaḥ sasadasyebhyo ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ tebhyaś ca pradadau vittaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: To the officiating priests and the assembled members of the council who had gathered there, he gave wealth in hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: lohitākṣāya sūtāya tathā sthapataye vibhuḥ yenoktaṃ tatra satrāgre yajñasya vinivartanam
english: To Lohitākṣa the Sūta, and likewise to the architect, the mighty king gave a great gift — it was he who had foretold at the very start of the sacrifice that it would be stopped.

sanskrit: nimittaṃ brāhmaṇa iti tasmai vittaṃ dadau bahu tataś cakārāvabhṛthaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Saying, 'This brahmin was the omen,' he gave him abundant wealth; then he performed the concluding ablution in accordance with the prescribed ritual.

sanskrit: āstīkaṃ preṣayām āsa gṛhān eva susatkṛtam rājā prītamanāḥ prītaṃ kṛtakṛtyaṃ manīṣiṇam
english: The king, his heart pleased, sent Āstīka — the wise one, pleased and fulfilled in his purpose — home with great honor.

sanskrit: punarāgamanaṃ kāryam iti cainaṃ vaco 'bravīt bhaviṣyasi sadasyo me vājimedhe mahākratau
english: And he said to him: You must come again; you shall be a member of my council at the great horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: tathety uktvā pradudrāva sa cāstīko mudā yutaḥ kṛtvā svakāryam atulaṃ toṣayitvā ca pārthivam
english: Saying 'So be it,' Āstīka departed joyfully, having accomplished an incomparable purpose and having satisfied the king.

sanskrit: sa gatvā paramaprīto mātaraṃ mātulaṃ ca tam abhigamyopasaṃgṛhya yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayat
english: He went, supremely glad, approached his mother and his maternal uncle, embraced them, and reported to them everything that had transpired.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā prīyamāṇāḥ sametā; ye tatrāsan pannagā vītamohāḥ te ''stīke vai prītimanto babhūvur; ūcuś cainaṃ varam iṣṭaṃ vṛṇīṣva
english: Hearing this, the serpents who had gathered there, freed from delusion and rejoicing, were filled with delight toward Āstīka; and they spoke to him: Choose whatever boon you desire.

sanskrit: bhūyo bhūyaḥ sarvaśas te 'bruvaṃs taṃ; kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāmo 'dya vidvan prītā vayaṃ mokṣitāś caiva sarve; kāmaṃ kiṃ te karavāmo 'dya vatsa
english: Again and again they all said to him on every side: What shall we do today that is dear to you, O wise one? We are pleased, and all of us have been saved; what desire shall we fulfill for you today, dear child?

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca sāyaṃ prātaḥ suprasannātmarūpā; loke viprā mānavāś cetare 'pi dharmākhyānaṃ ye vadeyur mamedaṃ; teṣāṃ yuṣmadbhyo naiva kiṃ cid bhayaṃ syāt
english: Āstīka said: May those in the world — brahmins, ordinary men, and others too — who with pure hearts morning and evening recite this account of mine have no fear from you whatsoever.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca taiś cāpy ukto bhāgineyaḥ prasannair; etat satyaṃ kāmam evaṃ carantaḥ prītyā yuktā īpsitaṃ sarvaśas te; kartāraḥ sma pravaṇā bhāgineya
english: The Sūta said: And addressed by them with pure hearts, their nephew was told: This is true; we who act thus with joy shall certainly fulfill every desire of yours, O nephew, being ever inclined to it.

sanskrit: jaratkāror jaratkārvāṃ samutpanno mahāyaśāḥ āstīkaḥ satyasaṃdho māṃ pannagebhyo 'bhirakṣatu
english: May Āstīka, born of Jaratkāru from Jaratkārvā, of great renown, firm in his vow of truth, protect me from serpents.

sanskrit: asitaṃ cārtimantaṃ ca sunīthaṃ cāpi yaḥ smaret divā vā yadi vā rātrau nāsya sarpabhayaṃ bhavet
english: Whoever remembers Asita, Ārtimanta, and Sunītha — whether by day or by night — shall have no fear of serpents.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mokṣayitvā sa bhujagān sarpasatrād dvijottamaḥ jagāma kāle dharmātmā diṣṭāntaṃ putrapautravān
english: The Sūta said: Having freed the serpents from the snake sacrifice, that best of twice-born, righteous in soul, went in time to his appointed end, blessed with sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: ity ākhyānaṃ mayāstīkaṃ yathāvat kīrtitaṃ tava yat kīrtayitvā sarpebhyo na bhayaṃ vidyate kva cit
english: Thus has the tale of Āstīka been recounted to you by me faithfully; one who narrates it has no fear from serpents anywhere.

sanskrit: śrutvā dharmiṣṭham ākhyānam āstīkaṃ puṇyavardhanam āstīkasya kaver vipra śrīmaccaritam āditaḥ
english: Having heard this most righteous tale of Āstīka — the meritorious story of the poet Āstīka, O brahmin, his glorious career from the very beginning —

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca bhṛguvaṃśāt prabhṛty eva tvayā me kathitaṃ mahat ākhyānam akhilaṃ tāta saute prīto 'smi tena te
english: Śaunaka said: The great tale has been told to me by you in full, O son of the Sūta, my dear — from the lineage of Bhṛgu onward; I am pleased with you for that.

sanskrit: prakṣyāmi caiva bhūyas tvāṃ yathāvat sūtanandana yāṃ kathāṃ vyāsasaṃpannāṃ tāṃ ca bhūyaḥ pracakṣva me
english: And I shall question you further, O delight of the Sūta; tell me also again the story composed by Vyāsa.

sanskrit: tasmin paramaduṣprāpe sarpasatre mahātmanām karmāntareṣu vidhivat sadasyānāṃ mahākave
english: During the intervals of that most difficult of rites — the snake sacrifice of those great souls — according to proper procedure, among the members of the council, O great poet —

sanskrit: yā babhūvuḥ kathāś citrā yeṣv artheṣu yathātatham tvatta icchāmahe śrotuṃ saute tvaṃ vai vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: Whatever wonderful stories arose and in what matters they were told truly — I wish to hear these from you, O Sūta, for you are indeed discerning.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca karmāntareṣv akathayan dvijā vedāśrayāḥ kathāḥ vyāsas tv akathayan nityam ākhyānaṃ bhārataṃ mahat
english: The Sūta said: During the intervals of the rite, the twice-born men told stories rooted in the Vedas; but Vyāsa always narrated the great tale, the Mahābhārata.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca mahābhāratam ākhyānaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ yaśaskaram janamejayena yat pṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā
english: Śaunaka said: The tale of the Mahābhārata, that account glorifying the Pāṇḍavas — when Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana was questioned by Janamejaya —

sanskrit: śrāvayām āsa vidhivat tadā karmāntareṣu saḥ tām ahaṃ vidhivat puṇyāṃ śrotum icchāmi vai kathām
english: He recited it in due form during those intervals of the rite; that sacred story I truly wish to hear in proper order.

sanskrit: manaḥsāgarasaṃbhūtāṃ maharṣeḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ kathayasva satāṃ śreṣṭha na hi tṛpyāmi sūtaja
english: Narrate it — that story born from the ocean of the great seer's mind, whose deeds are holy — O best among the righteous; I am never satiated, O son of the Sūta.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi mahad ākhyānam uttamam kṛṣṇadvaipāyanamataṃ mahābhāratam āditaḥ
english: The Sūta said: Very well, I shall tell you that great and excellent story — the Mahābhārata as composed by Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana — from the very beginning.

sanskrit: taj juṣasvottamamate kathyamānaṃ mayā dvija śaṃsituṃ tan manoharṣo mamāpīha pravartate
english: Enjoy it as I narrate it, O brahmin of supreme understanding; in recounting it, joy of mind arises within me here as well.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śrutvā tu sarpasatrāya dīkṣitaṃ janamejayam abhyāgacchad ṛṣir vidvān kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā
english: The Sūta said: Having heard that Janamejaya had consecrated himself for the snake sacrifice, the learned seer Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana then came to him.

sanskrit: janayām āsa yaṃ kālī śakteḥ putrāt parāśarāt kanyaiva yamunādvīpe pāṇḍavānāṃ pitāmaham
english: The one whom Kālī — still a maiden — bore on the island in the Yamunā from Parāśara, son of Śakti, that grandfather of the Pāṇḍavas —

sanskrit: jātamātraś ca yaḥ sadya iṣṭyā deham avīvṛdhat vedāṃś cādhijage sāṅgān setihāsān mahāyaśāḥ
english: Who, even as soon as he was born, instantly grew in body by the power of his will, and mastered the Vedas with all their ancillary branches and histories — that one of great glory —

sanskrit: yaṃ nātitapasā kaś cin na vedādhyayanena ca na vratair nopavāsaiś ca na prasūtyā na manyunā
english: Whom no one could surpass in austerity, nor in the study of the Vedas, nor by vows, nor by fasting, nor by birth, nor by ardor —

sanskrit: vivyāsaikaṃ caturdhā yo vedaṃ vedavidāṃ varaḥ parāvarajño brahmarṣiḥ kaviḥ satyavrataḥ śuciḥ
english: Who divided the one Veda into four — he, the best of those who know the Vedas, knower of the far and near, a brahmin seer, a poet, firm in the vow of truth, and pure —

sanskrit: yaḥ pāṇḍuṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca viduraṃ cāpy ajījanat śaṃtanoḥ saṃtatiṃ tanvan puṇyakīrtir mahāyaśāḥ
english: Who fathered Pāṇḍu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Vidura as well, extending the lineage of Śāntanu — he of holy fame and great glory —

sanskrit: janamejayasya rājarṣeḥ sa tad yajñasadas tadā viveśa śiṣyaiḥ sahito vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ
english: He entered the sacrificial hall of Janamejaya the royal seer at that time, accompanied by disciples who had mastered the Vedas and all their branches.

sanskrit: tatra rājānam āsīnaṃ dadarśa janamejayam vṛtaṃ sadasyair bahubhir devair iva puraṃdaram
english: There he saw King Janamejaya seated, surrounded by many members of the assembly — like Puraṃdara surrounded by the gods.

sanskrit: tathā mūrdhāvasiktaiś ca nānājanapadeśvaraiḥ ṛtvigbhir devakalpaiś ca kuśalair yajñasaṃstare
english: And also with consecrated kings from various countries, and with officiating priests equal to the gods, skilled in the spreading of the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: janamejayas tu rājarṣir dṛṣṭvā tam ṛṣim āgatam sagaṇo 'byudyayau tūrṇaṃ prītyā bharatasattamaḥ
english: Janamejaya the royal seer, best of the Bharatas, seeing that seer arrive, rose swiftly with his retinue out of joy.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ viṣṭaraṃ tasmai sadasyānumate prabhuḥ āsanaṃ kalpayām āsa yathā śakro bṛhaspateḥ
english: With the approval of the assembly members, the mighty king arranged a golden seat for him — just as Indra would for Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭaṃ varadaṃ devarṣigaṇapūjitam pūjayām āsa rājendraḥ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: When he had taken his seat there — the bestower of boons, honored by the hosts of divine seers — the foremost of kings honored him with acts prescribed by scripture.

sanskrit: pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca arghyaṃ gāṃ ca vidhānataḥ pitāmahāya kṛṣṇāya tadarhāya nyavedayat
english: Water for washing the feet, water for rinsing the mouth, the guest offering, and a cow — all in due order — he presented to Kṛṣṇa, his grandfather, as was worthy of him.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ pāṇḍavāj janamejayāt gāṃ caiva samanujñāya vyāsaḥ prīto 'bhavat tadā
english: Having received that honor from Janamejaya, the Pāṇḍava's descendant, and having given permission for the cow, Vyāsa was pleased at that time.

sanskrit: tathā saṃpūjayitvā taṃ yatnena prapitāmaham upopaviśya prītātmā paryapṛcchad anāmayam
english: Having thus honored that great-grandfather with care, the king sat near him with a joyful heart and inquired after his welfare.

sanskrit: bhagavān api taṃ dṛṣṭvā kuśalaṃ prativedya ca sadasyaiḥ pūjitaḥ sarvaiḥ sadasyān abhyapūjayat
english: The blessed one in turn, seeing the king, communicated his well-being, was honored by all the assembly members, and honored the assembly members in return.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ satkṛtaṃ sarvaiḥ sadasyair janamejayaḥ idaṃ paścād dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchat kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Then Janamejaya, after that best of twice-born had been duly honored by all the assembly members, thereafter addressed him with folded hands.
